## Root Cause: `flag_value` with `--flag/--no-flag` syntax is not supported and silently misbehaves

### 1. Where `flag_value` is processed

The logic lives in [`Option.__init__`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2533-L2624) in `src/click/core.py`.

### 2. The exact interaction between `flag_value` and `default`

Follow the execution order in `__init__`:

**Step A** — Capture whether `default` was explicitly passed ([line 2557]((/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2557))):
```python
default_is_missing = "default" not in attrs
```
`attrs` is a `**kwargs` dict. The check happens *before* `super().__init__()` is called.

**Step B** — `super().__init__()` is called ([line 2558]((/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2558-2560))), which stores `self.default` from `attrs`.

**Step C** — Determine `is_flag` ([lines 2590–2599](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2590-L2599)):
```python
if is_flag is None:
    if flag_value is not None:
        is_flag = True          # <-- triggered when flag_value=True is passed
    ...
    else:
        is_flag = bool(self.secondary_opts)  # <-- triggered by --verbose/--no-verbose
```
When you pass `flag_value=True`, `is_flag` is set to `True` here. `self.secondary_opts` (populated from `--no-verbose`) is **never consulted**.

**Step D** — Override `self.default` to `False` if `default_is_missing` ([lines 2607–2611](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2607-L2611)):
```python
if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:
    ...
    self.default = False
```
This only fires when `default` was **not** provided by the caller.

**Step E** — If `flag_value` is still `None`, derive it from `self.default` ([lines 2613–2614](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2613-L2614)):
```python
if is_flag and flag_value is None:
    flag_value = not self.default
```
This is the normal path for `--verbose/--no-verbose` (no explicit `flag_value`): `flag_value` becomes `not default`.

**Step F** — Compute `is_bool_flag` ([line 2623](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2623)):
```python
self.is_bool_flag: bool = is_flag and isinstance(self.type, types.BoolParamType)
```
When `flag_value=True` (a bool), the type resolves to `BoolParamType`, so `is_bool_flag=True`. When `flag_value` is e.g. `"upper"` (a string), `is_bool_flag=False`.

### 3. Why ordering matters and what actually breaks

**Case 1: `flag_value=True, default=True` (your first example)**

- `flag_value` is not `None` → `is_flag = True` (via Step C, first branch)
- `default_is_missing = False` → Step D is skipped, `self.default` stays `True`
- Step E is skipped (`flag_value` is not `None`)
- `is_bool_flag = True` (bool type)
- `self.secondary_opts` is set (from `--no-verbose`), but the code path for a bool flag with secondary opts adds both `--verbose` and `--no-verbose` to the parser ([line 2749](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2749-L2751)):

```python
if self.is_bool_flag and self.secondary_opts:
    parser.add_option(obj=self, dest=self.name, action="store_true", ...)
    parser.add_option(obj=self, dest=self.name, action="store_false", ...)
```

So `--no-verbose` *does* store `False`... but only if `is_bool_flag` ends up `True`. The **actual bug** is subtler: when you write `--verbose/--no-verbose, flag_value=True`, `flag_value` is redundant (it equals the value `--verbose` would naturally store), and the behavior is correct: `--no-verbose` sets the value to `False`. This is **not** the broken case.

**Case 2: `flag_value=True, default=True` where there are NO secondary opts**

If you write `@click.option('--verbose', flag_value=True, default=True)` (single opt), then:
- `is_flag = True` (Step C, because `flag_value is not None`)
- `is_bool_flag = True`
- `self.secondary_opts` is empty → the parser only adds `--verbose` as `store_true`
- There is no `--no-verbose` to set `False`; the flag always stores `True` when passed, and the default is `True` when omitted — it can never be `False`

**Case 3: `default=True, flag_value=True` (your second example — same kwargs, different order)**

Python `**kwargs` dictionaries are insertion-ordered but `option()` receives them as named parameters, so the **Python parameter order does not affect behavior**. Both calls produce *identical* `Option` objects. If you observe different runtime behavior, it is caused by something else (e.g. decorator stacking order, a different option name being used in one test, or a cached import).

### Summary

| Scenario | `is_flag` source | `flag_value` | `is_bool_flag` | `--no-verbose` works? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--verbose/--no-verbose` (no `flag_value`) | `bool(secondary_opts)` | `not default` | `True` | Yes |
| `--verbose/--no-verbose, flag_value=True` | `flag_value is not None` | `True` (explicit) | `True` | Yes (same path) |
| `--verbose, flag_value=True, default=True` | `flag_value is not None` | `True` (explicit) | `True` | No `--no-verbose` exists |

**The real issue:** mixing `--flag/--no-flag` syntax with an explicit `flag_value=True` is redundant and not the intended API. `flag_value` is designed for **non-boolean** flag groups (e.g. `--upper`/`--lower` sharing the same destination, as shown in the [docs example](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/docs/options.md?L317-L327)). For `--verbose/--no-verbose`, omit `flag_value` entirely and set only `default=True`:

```python
@click.option('--verbose/--no-verbose', default=True)
```

Click will automatically set `flag_value = not self.default = False` for `--no-verbose` via [line 2614](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/click--8.2.1/-/blob/src/click/core.py?L2614), and the secondary opt will store `False` correctly.
